title: The Cloud Watchers' Surprise
markdown:
The village fair was coming, and Iris, Button, and Professor Elm were so excited. They had planned games, yummy honey cake, and watching fireflies. But oh dear, big grey clouds were gathering, and the square already smelled of rain that had not quite decided to arrive.

Button’s ears drooped. “Will the fair be inside?”

Iris frowned. “I hope not. It’s better outside, under the sun.”

Professor Elm, the wise owl, hooted softly. “Let’s not worry. The sky tells stories.” He pointed up. “See those fluffy white clouds, like sheep? Those are cumulus clouds. They often mean a sunny day.”

Iris and Button leaned in, eyes wide. “And those thin streaks high up?” asked Button.

“Ah, cirrus clouds,” Professor Elm explained. “Made of ice crystals, far away. They might hint at changing weather, but usually mean it’s still bright.” He pointed to a dark cloud. “But those big dark nimbus clouds carry rain. They look like they hold full parcels of water.”

Iris’s mind whirred. “So,” she said, a hopeful smile blooming, “if we see lots of fluffy cumulus clouds and few dark nimbus clouds, the fair can stay outside?”

Professor Elm blinked kindly. “Precisely, clever Iris. You are learning the sky’s quiet language.”

They watched together, feeling the gentle breeze. They did not hurry the watching. Iris sat on the warm stone step. Button’s ears lifted a little, just to listen. Professor Elm’s feathers held a small square of sun. A bee crossed the square as if the sky had nothing to do with honey cake. The grey parcels drifted, and the sheep-clouds kept being sheep. Then, slowly, the dark nimbus clouds drifted apart. More soft white cumulus clouds appeared, floating peacefully across widening blue.

“Look!” Button exclaimed, full of relief. “The fluffy clouds are winning! They’re chasing the grey ones away!”

Iris beamed. “That means sunshine! The fair can stay outside!”

Professor Elm ruffled his feathers. “You have learned to read the sky, my little explorers. By noticing shapes and colours, you can guess the weather. It’s a beautiful puzzle, and you solved it.”

Button nudged Iris happily. “We used the clouds to plan our fun!”

Iris smiled, looking up at the vast sky. “It’s amazing what you learn by watching,” she whispered, a quiet wonder filling her.

As the sun warmed the earth and the last grey clouds faded like a whispered secret, they knew the fair would be magical. Tiny stars began to softly prick the velvet sky. Iris wondered what other stories the sky was still telling—another sheep, another parcel, another quiet language waiting for tomorrow’s fair.
characters: Iris (puzzle solver), Button (droopy-eared badger), Elm (sky-reading owl)
author: StoryGen Community
